newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian Azomures halted from trading.
newsitem.headline: Romanian Azomures halted from trading.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Monday fertiliser maker Azomures SA would be suspended from trading on Thursday following a split of its shares.
Each Azomures share registered in the exchange's registry with a nominal value of 25,000 lei will be divided into 25 shares of 1,000 lei each, a bourse statement said.

The share split follows oversubscription in a mass selloff, launched late in 1995, offering Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in 4,000 state companies in exchange for coupons. The Azomures stake on offer was around 30 percent.
A 51 percent stake in the company was sold off last week to a Romanian trading company by Azomures' former majority stockholder -- the State Ownership Fund.
Azomures is the second stock to make a share split after oil drilling company Foraj Sonde SA.
The suspension is meant to allow investors to digest the news and reconsider prices in line with the new nominal value.

Azomures, based in the Transylvanian town of Tirgu Mures has a share capital of 209.4 billion lei. The bourse said Azomures had recently raised its capital from a previous 172 billion lei after adding the value of terrain to it.
The market price of Azomures split shares will be set by demand and offer when it rejoins trading, with the new quote being the following session's reference price, the bourse said.
Brokers anticipate a new Azomures price of some 1,500 lei.
It is the only of Bucharest bourse listed stock trading on the first tier, where qualification criteria are tougher.
The second tier will trade 18 stocks starting Tuesday when two more companies are expected to join in trading.
Azomures has been a key attraction in trading since it joined the market a year ago due to sound financial results and high liquidity. It closed last week 2,200 lei higher at 29,900. ($=6,183 lei)
